doc.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018

title: Gospel choir with Daryl Coley, then auditions and demos
summary: She found her voice in Daryl Coley's Oakland choir, then after acting school decided to tour like the singer Annie Lennox called, and did demos.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: So you wanted to be — I mean you aspired to go beyond that? Or did it just sort of happen?

No I mean I wanted to work. So probably in my early twenties I think, when I was starting to audition for shows and things like that in New York. I didn’t know what I wanted to do. I just knew, all right I had some Gospel. I was raised Presbyterian so I was not raised in the Baptist church, but I loved Gospel music. So I moved out to the west coast when I was in my teens, and one thing led to another and I was able to join a Gospel choir led by the great Reverend Daryl Coley, who was a star in the Gospel music industry, a Stellar Award winner. And he was working along with — he had his own group which was the New Generation Singers, which was the group I joined. And I’m talking about the Bay Area now, in Oakland, in the mid-seventies. And he worked along with the Hawkins family, who were a big pioneering family, a Gospel group of the contemporary Gospel field, not the traditional field. And so that’s kind of where I found my voice you know, and I said, “Oh okay. Maybe my voice is a little bigger than I think it is, or maybe.” So he was the one that really pushed me to get out front. Because I was very content in the choir, in the alto section of the choir. And he just said, “No, today” you know, not today, but, “the next performance we do you’re going to lead a song.” And I said, “Why?” “Because I want you to sing this. I think you can sing this.” So that was really my first experience singing with all these voices behind me and having to really get my voice out there. So then after that I said well maybe I should try — I moved back to New York and went to acting school and said maybe I should try to audition. You know, I don’t know if I’m going to get a job but maybe I should try to do that. So then I was sitting at an audition one day — these are long answers to short questions I hope that’s okay — and one of the other girls came in. She said, “Annie Lennox called me on the phone.” I said — I thought, how do you get Annie Lennox? How does that happen? So I filed that away and I said that’s what I want to do. I want to tour. I want to travel, and I want to be able to say that some day. So-and-so called me on the phone. I’ll never forget it, when she walked in and I’m waiting, the three of us are sitting there waiting to audition. And I thought how does — okay, that’s it, that’s my mission. So then after that, you know this and that happened, I start doing demos for people, and Tom McGrath was one of those people, like he started calling, the New York network type thing.
